correctness.rationale: For all labeled simple cycles n>=3, the proof verifies the exact normalized utility, eliminates disconnected and singleton coalitions by strict welfare-improving moves, proves every path block of size>=5 can be improved by splitting off three vertices (gap at least 1/10 at size five), optimizes the 2/3/4 block counts by the congruence t=2a+c, and compares explicit cycle grand welfare against proper partitions using a positive monotone gap after n=6. Cyclic block arrangements are counted without rotational quotient. Exact rational DP, cyclic-cut enumeration and all unrestricted partitions at small n passed; no finite test substitutes for the all-n proof.

value.rationale: Cycles form the first minimal connected non-tree graph family for the canonical induced-distance coalitional game. The theorem gives an exact optimizer and counts every optimum at arbitrary order, resolves whether closing a path into a ring changes the grand-coalition incentive, and proves the sharp 6-to-7 fragmentation transition. The output is a natural complete classification with an explicit linear-time construction, not a disconnected fixed-size numerical table. The many-optima counts are relevant to choosing among socially efficient coalition organizations.
